clues.text: Jesus told of a merchant who found one very precious one and sold all he had to buy it.
In John's vision of the new Jerusalem, each of the twelve gates was made from a single one.
Jesus taught not to give dogs what is holy, nor to throw these where they would be trampled underfoot.
At King Xerxes' feast in Susa, the mosaic pavement held porphyry, marble, and a shell material named after this.
Paul wanted women to adorn themselves with modesty, not with braided hair, gold, these, or costly garments.
In John's vision, the woman dressed in purple and scarlet was adorned with gold, precious stones, and these.
In John's vision, a cargo list naming gold, silver, silk, citron wood, and ivory also included these.
